name: Henry's Fork (Box Canyon)
blurb: Island Park Dam to Last Chance — a short basalt canyon on some of the most famous trout water in the West.

sections.notes: Launch at the Box Canyon boat ramp below Island Park Dam and take out at Last Chance. This is rocky moving water; releases and low water change the trip. Give wading anglers room and confirm the takeout before starting. Check current access and fishing rules before extending beyond Last Chance.

distanceEvidence.note: Approximate published reach length from the guide currently linked by HFF. It is independent of the facility coordinates and is not a surveyed landing-to-landing distance. Channel choice and reservoir conditions can change the actual trip.

notices.title: Use the below-dam launch
notices.text: The Box Canyon boat ramp is a different facility from the Island Park Reservoir ramps and the hike-in campground access. This itinerary ends at Last Chance.
notices.sourceName: Henry’s Fork Foundation — upper-river access guide

putInAccess.accessType: Public boat ramp below Island Park Dam
putInAccess.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
putInAccess.note: IDFG point is in the parking loop, set back from the ramp. The HFF upper-river guide, page 45, and USFS boat-ramp inventory independently identify this below-dam boating access.
putInAccess.directions: Use the Box Canyon boat ramp BELOW Island Park Dam, not a ramp on Island Park Reservoir or the hike-in campground access. Identify the ramp from the parking area before unloading.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
takeOutAccess.note: IDFG point lies in parking near the bank, consistent with the HFF upper-river guide, page 52. It does not establish the water-edge ramp position.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the signed Last Chance boat ramp and designated day-use parking. Confirm this takeout before launching from Box Canyon; the marker identifies the facility rather than the exact shoreline landing.

timing.note: The former reference speed has no documented trip calibration. The live gauge and published four-mile reach remain useful, but they do not establish a reliable live travel-time estimate.

mapAuditNote: Named facilities, published guide distances and satellite imagery reviewed. Approved sections show approximate access areas; exact shoreline connections and route geometry are separate reviews.
